newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan's Bhutto wants brother's body exhumed.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan's Bhutto wants brother's body exhumed.

text.p: Former Pakistani prime minister Benazir Bhutto called on Sunday for the body of her estranged younger brother Murtaza to be exhumed to determine exactly who killed him during a police shootout last September.

She told a three-judge inquiry it was necessary to exhume the body to ascertain who fired the first bullet that wounded and killed Murtaza on September 20 near his home in Karachi's seaside Clifton district.

Members of a Murtaza-led breakaway faction of Bhutto's Pakistan People's Party (PPP) accuse the former prime minister's husband Asif Ali Zardari of conspiring to murder their leader. Zardari, who has been in jail since his wife was sacked as prime minister last November, denies the charge.

Bhutto said private British detectives whom her government had engaged to investigate the matter had favoured exhumation and that a tentative report by them had found that the first shot was fired by a Murtaza bodyguard, Sajjad Gakhro.
"All this you can only verify when you exhume the body and get the exact bullets," Bhutto said.
She said it would be painful to exhume the body "but it is more painful if you don't know the facts. I want to know who killed my brother."
On the first day of her testimony on Saturday, Bhutto had said Murtaza's killing was part of a conspiracy to oust her government.

Bhutto, who will continue the testimony on Tuesday, repeated her charges that Leghari had waged psychological warfare against her before sacking her three-year-old government on November 5 on disputed charges of corruption and misrule.
Leghari denies that he had conspired to remove Bhutto, who got him elected as president after the 1993 general elections, which were won by the PPP.

Bhutto's father and then-prime minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto was toppled in a 1977 army coup and executed in 1979 after a controversial conviction for conspiring to murder a political opponent, and her youngest brother Shahnawaz died of suspected poisoning in France in 1985.
The PPP was routed in the February 3 elections by new Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's Pakistan Muslim League party.
